MINUTES

  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING

  FEBRUARY 23, 2016

An adjourned meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called
to order at 5:00 p.m. in the City Manager’s Office, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZUCKERMAN for the purpose of interviewing Committee applicants.

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:00 p.m. in the City Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL
City Council Members Present: Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
City Council Member Absent:  Mitchell

City Staff Present:  City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Planning Director David Wahba

Others Present:  Ritu Portugal, Park and Activities Commission

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  WASTE MANAGEMENT DRAWING FOR ONE YEAR’S FREE RESIDENTIAL
  REFUSE SERVICE

  Janine Hamner, Community Affairs, introduced Angelica Dulce, Community
  Liaison, Waste Management.

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, Ms. Hamner noted that the City of
  Manhattan Beach has instituted a program for food recycling and composting.
  Additionally, Ms. Hamner pointed out that all restaurants that generate a
  specific amount of food waste must now comply with AB 1826.

  Ms. Dulce drew the name of Judy and Richard Borsuk, Pinto Lane, as the
  recipient of one year’s free disposal service.

5.  ROUTINE MATTERS

A.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 9, 2016

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE THE CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 9, 2016 AS
  PRESENTED.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – JANUARY AND FEBRUARY

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE WARRANTS 56444 THROUGH 56477 FOR A GRAND
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $154,149.74 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
FEBRUARY 23, 2016
 6.  CONSENT CALENDAR: The following routine matters will be acted upon by one
  vote to approve with the majority consent of the City Council. There will be no
  separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior
  to the roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO APPROVE ITEMS A-C.

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  Reading in full of all ordinances and resolutions presented for consideration to the
  City Council will be waived and all such ordinances and resolutions will be read
  by title only.

  APPROVED.

B.  JANUARY 2016 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

C.  JANUARY MONTHLY REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

7.  AUDIENCE ITEMS  NOT  ON  THE  AGENDA/WRITTEN  AND  ORAL
  COMMUNICATIONS

A.  Don Hinshilwood, 40 Encanto, explained a situation involving his next door
  neighbor burning wood in an outdoor fireplace noting that the smoke travels
  directly into their home. He then referred to the City of Torrance’s ordinance that
  bans open flames, including fire pits, and asked for the COUNCIL’S consideration
  to adopt a similar ordinance.

  Because Mr. Hinshilwood lives in the same neighborhood as COUNCILWOMAN
  HUFF, she noted that this issue was discussed at their recent homeowners’
  association meeting, and they decided that this matter is not within their purview.
  She then suggested that a mediator might be beneficial to address this complaint.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN, Planning Director Wahba stated
  that the Air Quality Management District (AQMD) had been contacted, but was
  unresponsive. He then suggested Mr. Hinshilwood contact COUNCILWOMAN
  MITCHELL as she is a member on the AQMD Board.

  After further discussion, City Manager Prichard suggested that staff work with the
  AQMD and COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL to see if there is any regulation that is
  being violated.

B.  Ken Lieu, 5114 Kingspine, explained his situation where he was told that he was
  in violation of City ordinance by installing artificial turf in the City’s right-of-way.
  He distributed before and after pictures of his home and suggested that the City
  provide waiver forms that allow this type of installation.

  Planning Director Wahba provided some background stating that he was notified
  by Rockbluff Homeowners’ Association President Judy Bayer that this turf was in
  place. He noted that at the meeting of December 8, COUNCIL gave clear direction
  that artificial turf was not allowed in the public right-of-way and enforcement
  measures should be undertaken.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF inquired about the cost Mr. Lieu incurred installing the
  turf in the right-of-way. He stated that it was approximately $2,000.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
FEBRUARY 23, 2016
   MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN inquired if the actual Notice of Violation was issued
  and what remedy should be followed. Planning Director Wahba noted that there
  is an appeal process that begins with a notice, a $100 fine, and then the resident
  can appeal the citation.

  City Attorney Davis noted that the appeal process is handled administratively and
  cautioned the COUNCIL not to intervene at this point.

  City Manager Prichard advised the COUNCIL, with respect to the right-of-way,
  that an ordinance already exists that approves certain landscaping in the City’s
  rights-of-way.

  Mr. Lieu emphasized that his artificial turf is high quality and enhances the
  neighborhood.

  City Manager Prichard noted that staff looks for solutions that are satisfactory to
  both the City and resident. He further noted that the COUNCIL has always
  attempted to make sure that the public feels like they are being heard.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS/MEETINGS

A.  CONTINUED PUBLIC HEARING - PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 02-16
  (ORDINANCE NO. 704) (PROHIBITION AGAINST MARIJUANA CULTIVATION AND
  MEDICAL MARIJUANA DELIVERY); APPLICANT: CITY OF ROLLING HILLS
  ESTATES; LOCATION: CITY-WIDE

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Take public testimony; 2) Discuss
  the issues; 3) Close the public hearing; and 4) Conduct the second reading and
  adopt Ordinance No. 704.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  No public testimony was offered.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING AND ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 704.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Mitchell

  City Manager Prichard read Ordinance No. 704 by title only.

9.  NEW BUSINESS

  NONE

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-29-07; APPLICANT: CHADMAR HOMES AND
  ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB; LOCATION 26311 AND 27000 PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE EAST; REQUEST TO USE NORTHEAST CORNER OF PALOS VERDES
  DRIVE NORTH AND EAST FOR TEMPORARY PARKING LOT; AND OTHER
  ISSUES RELATED TO THE PROJECT’S DEVELOPMENT, INCLUDING A BRIDLE
  TRAIL ALONG PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST TO LOMITA RESERVOIR

  Recommendation: That the City Council provide further direction to staff and the
  applicant with respect to the proposed request for temporary parking on the
  corner of Palos Verdes Drive North and Palos Verdes Drive East and the other
  related items listed in the report.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
FEBRUARY 23, 2016
   COUNCILWOMAN HUFF noted the Montecillo Homeowners’ Association’s concern
  about delaying development of the park.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN HUFF, Planning Director Wahba noted that the
  City can set the term of the parking agreement with the Country Club to expire
  August, 2017 whether or not the project is completed. He further noted that the
  proposed park funding is already in place from Quimby funds.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF inquired if there is a current plan in place for the park.
  Planning Director Wahba noted that initial discussion has taken place at the Park
  and Activities Commission where conceptual suggestions were made that
  included a passive park, play equipment, benches, etc.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF noted that on behalf of the Montecillo neighborhood,
  they would like to see the park move forward. Planning Director Wahba noted
  that the Park and Activities Commission could consider this concept now and
  discuss how the Country Club would assist in this plan in the future.

  City Manager Prichard suggested that whatever agreement is reached, an “out”
  clause could be included for the park development and that the COUNCIL would
  approve the final design.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN thanked Chadmar and the Country Club
  representatives for their collaboration on this matter with regards to the width of
  the trails. He noted that June’s Trail would have a minimum 15 foot width. He
  further suggested reviewing drainage issues on this trail. Additionally, he
  commented that the trail at the end of Dapplegray behind the homes is
  particularly troublesome and would like the Country Club to make it a more
  natural setting. Planning Director Wahba noted that he will work with the
  Country Club and Chadmar on these issue.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN then referred to the parking matter and stated that
  allowing the temporary parking is part of being neighborly as the Country Club
  has been in the community for many years. He noted that he did not wish to
  impose a fee for using the parking lot and believed this approval will benefit the
  Country Club and City. Finally, he stated that he is reluctant to move forward
  with the proposed park before the entire Casaba development is completed.

  Chuck Lande, Chadmar Group, cautioned the COUNCIL about certain
  expectations when work is taking place on someone else’s property due to liability
  issues. He further noted that the Dapplegray Lane Property Owners’ Association
  does not own the land where the trail is located, but while acknowledging that
  these issues are important, he stated that what was presented in the staff report
  is what they intend to follow. He then stated that June’s Trail does need to be
  addressed to make sure it drains properly.

  Mr. Lande further noted his concern with the language being used regarding this
  issue and the need to improve landscaping of the easement subject to the
  COUNCIL approving the agreements. MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN responded
  that staff is not expecting the Country Club to rebuild the trail, but rather retain
  the integrity of the landscaping.

  Planning Director Wahba clarified the City’s goals and responsibilities with respect
  to the drainage. He further noted that acquisition of an easement traversing
  through certain other of the Dapplegray and Sorrell trails may be necessary to
  control the drainage.

  City Manager Prichard noted that separate easements for the horse trail and
  drainage maintenance may also be necessary and will discuss this issue with the
  City’s engineer for input on the final design.

  Planning Director Wahba noted that the COUNCIL will review the larger picture at
  the Policy Development Session.

  Mr. Lande commented that the need for temporary parking for the Country Club
  is crucial since they will not have any parking available until the clubhouse is
  completed.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
FEBRUARY 23, 2016
   Jerry Gliksman Dapplegray Lane Property Owners’ Association, commented that
  they did not agree with what was previously discussed. He noted areas affecting
  Dapplegray include June’s Trail, the easements on Lots 113-119, and the need for
  a documented plan from the Country Club, Chadmar, and the City. He further
  noted that a promise was made several years ago that the aforementioned trails
  were going to be cleaned up.

  Mr. Lande stated that there are no recorded easements along June’s Trail on the
  southern boundary.

  Ritu Portugal commented that in terms of the parking lot, she is a resident on
  Clubview Lane and was in support of allowing the Country Club to use City
  property on Palos Verdes Drive North and Palos Verdes Drive East.

  Mrs. Portugal noted that the Park and Activities Commission, of which she is a
  member, reviewed the proposed park plan that had very little detail. She further
  noted that they are considering playground equipment.

  Mr. Gliksman reiterated that written documentation must be provided and
  recommended that the COUNCIL retain a surveyor to figure out where the 12½
  foot trail is located, and if an additional two and a half feet would be beneficial, for
  the City to take action.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that 15 feet will be provided for the trail.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that City Attorney Davis can work with staff
  to create sufficient documentation.

  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF reiterated the Montecillo Homeowners’ Association’s
  concern about delaying the park since their neighborhood will be impacted the
  most.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted her support of the parking lot until August,
  2017. She further noted that it would be of benefit to those residents on Clubview
  to allow this use.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN concurred with this timeline and having to wait another
  couple of months for the park should not be a problem if the site is properly
  conditioned.

  COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ noted that having a park next to a construction site
  would not be desirable.

  After extensive discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to allow the
  Country Club to use that corner for the period requested.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired if the COUNCIL was interested in receiving
  compensation from the Country Club on this issue.

  After brief discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL not to pursue
  payment for this use.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN urged staff to work with the Country Club to
  determine what their capabilities will be in terms of vacating that site and how the
  City would benefit.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN SCHMITZ, Planning Director Wahba noted that
  he will work with the City Attorney in regards to the Country Club “helping” the
  City with the park.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN suggested that a scope of work outlining what the City will
  do to move forward would be desirable.

  In response to City Manager Prichard, Planning Director Wahba noted that he will
  work with the Country Club’s attorney in an effort to create some basic conditions
  of approval, i.e. license agreement. He further noted that these issues will be
  addressed at the March 22 COUNCIL meeting, but retention of a consultant
  would be necessary to review the drainage on June’s Trail.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
FEBRUARY 23, 2016
   In response to City Manager Prichard, Planning Director Wahba responded that a
  public hearing to amend the Conditional Use Permit would be required and will
  notice that for the March 22 meeting.

  City Manager Prichard recommended that the applicant reimburse the City for
  City Attorney Davis’ time since there will be a substantial amount of work
  involved. It was the consensus of the COUNCIL to accept this recommendation.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN asked everyone to act in the spirit of collaboration
  and cooperation.

  It was the consensus of the COUNCIL:

  TO STAFF TO: 1) WORK WITH THE CITY ATTORNEY AND APPLICANT TO
  FORMULATE A LICENSE AGREEMENT (AND REIMBURSE THE CITY FOR
  HIS TIME); 2) WORK WITH ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB TO
  DETERMINE HOW THEY WILL ASSIST THE CITY WITH THE PROPOSED
  PARK AT THAT LOCATION; AND 3) PROVIDE A SCOPE OF WORK
  (INCLUDING DRAINAGE) OUTLINING WHAT THE CITY CAN DO TO MOVE
  THIS PROJECT FORWARD.

11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

A.  City Attorney Davis reiterated that the artificial turf issue raised previously must
  go through the administrative process before any action is taken.

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the
  opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and reports to
  other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of
  currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and
  their various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or
  have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

A.  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN reported that he attended an event sponsored by the
  Milliken Institute where discussion took place regarding how Australia handles
  their severe drought and how it relates to California.

13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members
  of the City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or
  issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration
  and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  NEW COMMISSION/COMMITTEE APPOINTMENTS – MAYOR ZUCKERMAN

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted that the COUNCIL interviewed several applicants for
  various Commission/Committee vacancies. After COUNCIL consensus, he
  announced the following appointments:

  Tim Thomas – Planning Commission
  Timothy Zigrang – Planning Commission
  Lisa Hawkins – Equestrian Committee
  Carrie Silvano – Equestrian Committee

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN also noted that he would call applicant Mel Aou to
  determine his interest in serving on the Park and Activities Commission.

  City Manager Prichard noted that there are still vacancies on the Park and
  Activities Commission, Environmental Advisory Committee and Traffic and Safety
  Committee. He encouraged anyone who is interested to contact Deputy City Clerk
  Hope Nolan for an application.

  After brief discussion, the COUNCIL decided it was not necessary to meet with
  those Planning Commissioners who did not attend a prior appointment.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
FEBRUARY 23, 2016
 B.  City Manager Prichard noted that the City received a letter requesting
  nominations for Older Americans Recognition Day.

  After brief discussion, it was the consensus of the COUNCIL to nominate former
  Park and Activities Commissioner Dale Allen.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN suggested sending Mr. Allen a letter informing him of this
  honor.

14.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  DISCUSSION WITH RESPECT TO PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT: QUARTERLY CITY
  MANAGER REVIEW

  NO ACTION WAS TAKEN.

15.  ADJOURNMENT

  At 10:15 p.m. MAYOR ZUCKERMAN formally adjourned the City Council
  meeting to Saturday, March 5, 2016 at 8:00 a.m. for the purpose of conducting
  the Policy Development Session.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Hope J. Nolan  Douglas R. Prichard
Deputy City Clerk  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
FEBRUARY 23, 2016
